PREDICTION REFUTED, in two dispatches, and the split is the finding.

FIRST DISPATCH -- verdict confirmed against the tool as it stood, basis refuted. `vit interface` emitted `INTEGER(C_INT), INTENT(INOUT) :: list(*)` plus `INTEGER(C_INT), VALUE :: n_list`, under a wrapper declaring `INTEGER(4), INTENT(INOUT) :: list(:)` -- the ALLOCATABLE attribute dropped with no diagnostic, although fortran_parser had recorded is_allocatable=True. Measured against the original on the live ROSCO path (allocate 4, append 3x): the caller's array was still 4 elements, the appended values written one past the end of its heap block, and nothing -- gfortran, g++, or the run -- said so. A hand-written Fortran 2018 CFI bridge reproduced the oracle BYTE FOR BYTE on both branches, so the limit was VIT's, not the argument's. evidence/AddToList/bridge_probe/result.json.

SECOND DISPATCH -- the verdict is refuted too. VIT 37f8bdf generates that bridge: the dummy is declared in the BIND(C) interface exactly as the original declares it (`DIMENSION(:), ALLOCATABLE, INTENT(INOUT)`), no extent parameter is emitted, and the C side receives the caller's own CFI_cdesc_t*. The unit is INTEGRATED on that path. Nothing about it is hand-written: interface block, wrapper, C++ scaffold, the differential harness's Fortran bridge and the post-integration shim are all generated (X1, X2). The loop's harness learned the same convention (cf885e3) -- three generators, which is what the escalation said it would take.

WHERE THE BASIS CAME FROM: tests/conformance/matrix.toml's `[c_alloc_inout] compiles = "no"` was measured from `test_validate.generate_fortran_bridge` -- the DIFFERENTIAL HARNESS's Fortran side, never linked into the library -- while `vit integrate` ships `interface_gen`'s output, which compiled clean and did nothing. The cell now reads compiles="yes", integrates="yes", re-measured. The prediction was right by luck of a different generator failing.

STILL REFUSED by VIT, for being UNMEASURED rather than impossible, each with its reason in the exception message: a SCALAR allocatable, rank >= 2, a CHARACTER or derived-type element, and any type/kind the interface cannot declare as the actual's own (LOGICAL, COMPLEX). The three other `bridge_feasible: no` entries waiting on this -- Read_OL_Input, ParseInAry_Opt, ParseDbAry_Opt -- are not thereby unblocked: their verdicts were derived from the same pre-`integrates` matrix and have to be re-measured, not inferred from this one.

bridge_feasible.observed:
PREDICTION NOW RESOLVED FOR THE INTEGRATION PATH. The first dispatch recorded that VIT REFUSES to generate anything for this unit, deterministically, because TYPE(ErrorVariables) carries `CHARACTER(:), ALLOCATABLE :: ErrMsg`. That refusal was correct and is now CLOSED, in VIT (a2e2c30), additively and red-tested.

A deferred-length CHARACTER has no C type, because its LENGTH is part of its allocation: reassigning it reallocates it, and C++ cannot reallocate Fortran's storage. It therefore crosses as THREE members -- a staging buffer the populator module owns, the current length, and the writable CAPACITY -- with the reallocating assignment performed by the reverse copy. The capacity is the member that makes the field writable rather than merely readable; without it the C++ cannot know how much room it has and `ErrVar%ErrMsg = RoutineName//':'//TRIM(ErrVar%ErrMsg)` could not be translated at all. Over-long assignment is REFUSED and reported, never truncated: a shortened error message is a plausible wrong answer, the one kind a bit comparison cannot catch.

`vit analyze-types --fix character`, the remedy VIT's own message suggested, is still REFUSED and now unnecessary. It rewrites ROSCO's type definition to a fixed length, changing LEN(ErrVar%ErrMsg), which sizes avcMSG, which is Record 49. P7.

MEASURED AFTER THE FIX: `vit translate ExtController` succeeds; `vit interface` emits all five arguments over a five-argument bridge -- read attribute by attribute against the original and matching, including REAL(4) for REAL(ReKi) (an explicit kind is not promoted by -fdefault-real-8). Generated view populators are committed at rosco/controller/src/vit_{controlparameters,localvariables,extcontroltype,errorvariables}_view.f90 and compile.

A SECOND VIT DEFECT FOUND ON THE WAY, RECORDED BEFORE IT WAS FIXED (C12), and much larger than this unit. `vit test-validate` emitted the differential bridge's dummy list on ONE LINE. Decomposing ControlParameters (214 fields) and LocalVariables (168) produced a SUBROUTINE statement 11,747 characters long; free-form Fortran's limit is 132 columns, so gfortran truncated it and reported 1,153 diagnostics, none of which named the cause. EVERY unit in this campaign taking either type -- most of ROSCO's controllers -- was outside `vit test-validate` entirely, and nothing said so. The campaign's first four units took scalars, arrays and strings and never touched a derived type, which is why it went unmeasured until here. Fixed in VIT (83d25f9) as a rule about line CONTENTS rather than a list of emission sites, because wrapping only the dummy list left the array copy-in statements at 133-153 columns. statemachine_bridge.f90 now compiles; the wrong artifact is kept at evidence/ExtController/vit_defects/.

STILL REFUSED, and this is what now blocks the unit: a deferred-length CHARACTER FIELD of a DECOMPOSED derived type, in `vit test-validate`. `_decomposed_param_names` classifies on is_allocatable first, so ErrMsg is routed to the array path and `get_type_mapping` raises. The fix is the same three-member shape already built for the view struct, one generator over.

SECOND BRIDGE, STILL NOT MEASURED: plan.json declares LoadDynamicLib a permanent bridge, and ExtController's SAVE local `DLL_Ext` is a TYPE(ExtDLL_Type) -- five fields including TYPE(C_FUNPTR) :: ProcAddr(3) and CHARACTER(1024) :: ProcName(3). It does not cross the signature, so it needs a production bridge that owns the SAVE state, not a view. X1 forbids inlining LoadDynamicLib to avoid it.

RESOLVED FOR THE DIFFERENTIAL PATH TOO, in VIT 8c34ceb. The refusal recorded above -- a deferred-length CHARACTER FIELD of a decomposed type -- is closed, as buffer + length + capacity, the same three members the view struct already used. Three more shapes had to change with it, and two of them were silent rather than refusing: a rank-1 ALLOCATABLE field and a SCALAR field of an INOUT argument were both INPUT-ONLY (no copy-back at all), and a LOGICAL field crossed as int32_t on one side and int8_t on the other. See `escalation`.

The ExtDLL_Type production bridge is BUILT: rosco/controller/src/vit_extcontroller_dll.f90 owns the SAVE TYPE(ExtDLL_Type), calls LoadDynamicLib (X1 -- it is called, not reproduced) and returns ProcAddr(1) as a C function pointer for the translation to call through, which is what C_F_PROCPOINTER compiles to. `ALLOCATE(ExtDLL%avrSWAP(max_avr_entries))` is NOT auto-extracted: vit/allocate_extract.py classifies it `local` because the size is a local PARAMETER, and `--auto-allocate`'s output does not compile on this codebase at all. See `escalation`.

units.observability:
THE GATE STILL CANNOT SEE THIS UNIT, AND THAT IS UNCHANGED AND STILL LOAD-BEARING.

ExtControl.f90 measures 0 of 28 EXECUTABLE lines in all 27 scenarios (evidence/ExtController/coverage_extcontrol.json prints 0/28 twenty-seven times; the denominator had to be regenerated because coverage/line_coverage.json stores only non-zero hit counts, so 'never ran' and 'never instrumented' are the same empty dictionary). Re-measured against the INTEGRATED Release build: making the unit a no-op moved 0 of 5,252,000 values, replacements: 1, revert_verified: true, residual_dirt: []. gate/ExtController.json's green constrains nothing and is committed beside gate/ExtController.redtest.json, which says so.

Nothing about that changes with the oracle fixture. DISCON.F90's own comment says it: 'Data from external dll is in ExtDLL%avrSWAP, it's unused in the following code'. Even a working external controller writes nothing the gate compares.

WHAT THE HARNESS CAN AND CANNOT SEE, stated rather than left to be found:
  SEEN   ExtDLL%avrSWAP (2000 elements and the extent itself), ErrVar%ErrStat, ErrVar%ErrMsg and its length, and every one of CntrPar's 286 decomposed parameters -- 448 compared outputs per case. The three length records the unit computes are read back by the oracle, and so are the bytes of accINFILE and avcOUTNAME and the incoming aviFAIL, because the fixture was extended to fold them in when it turned out they were reaching the library and never being read.
  NOT SEEN  (1) The `iStatus /= 0` path. harness/ranges.toml pins iStatus to 0, so the initialisation branch runs on every case and its ABSENCE is never exercised. The four statements it skips are the two DLL_Ext assignments, LoadDynamicLib, the ALLOCATE and four PRINTs; everything after END IF runs identically on both paths.
  (2) DLL_FileName and DLL_ProcName are held at one value each, so nothing here distinguishes a translation that reads them from one that ignores them. DLL_InFile is NOT pinned and is built by the same TRIM/TRANSFER shape, which is what keeps that code observable.
  (3) LEN_TRIM(ErrVar%ErrMsg) is 0 in every admissible case, because LoadDynamicLib blank-fills the message through a CHARACTER(*), INTENT(OUT) dummy. Two of the four declared-equivalent mutants are that.
  (4) LocalVar%ACC_INFILE is a CHARACTER ARRAY field, which the harness refuses rather than flattening; it is supplied as a zeroed buffer and not compared. This unit does not read it.

So the shape of the answer is unit #1's, one instrument further along: a DEAD unit closes on the harness and the mutation score, and the gate's green for it is evidence of nothing and is committed as such.

  A. `vit test-validate` crossing a deferred-length CHARACTER FIELD of a decomposed type -- DONE, VIT 8c34ceb, as buffer + length + capacity, the same three members a2e2c30 built for the view struct. This was the 37-of-69 blocker.
  B. The loop harness supplying CHARACTER fields -- DONE, loop 7d7c913. Both shapes cross (fixed-width and deferred-length); a CHARACTER ARRAY field is still refused, with its reason.
  C. The JUDGEMENT about what the harness may hold constant -- MADE, and written down where it can be reviewed: harness/ranges.toml, which is committed and states the measurement forcing each of its four pins. Every one exists because the REFERENCE crashes on the rest of the domain, not because the translation would: ExtController never checks ErrVar%ErrStat after LoadDynamicLib and calls through a null ProcAddr. That is a finding about upstream ROSCO and the file says so.

A FOURTH THING WAS FOUND ON THE WAY AND IS LARGER THAN ANY OF THEM (C12). The decomposed bridge copied every field IN and almost none OUT: a rank-1 ALLOCATABLE field and a SCALAR field of an INOUT argument were both input-only, so ExtDLL%avrSWAP -- this unit's principal output -- and ErrVar%ErrStat were supplied to the reference and then discarded. Every unit in this campaign taking a derived type was affected. The wrong artifact is kept at evidence/ExtController/vit_defects/extcontroller_bridge.alloc_input_only.f90.

Three defects, measured, artifact at evidence/ExtController/vit_defects/integrate_auto_allocate.wrapper.f90 -- its copy-call scan matches ANY `CALL x(..., arg%field, ...)` and hoisted BOTH LoadDynamicLib and the external DLL call into the wrapper; it declines a size expression that is a local PARAMETER; and its error handling emits SetErrStat and CHARACTER(ErrMsgLen), OpenFAST names that exist nowhere in ROSCO. COST PAID TO REACH 1.000, and it is a finding about the INSTRUMENT rather than about the unit. One `compare_op` mutant -- `if (CornerFreq < 0)` -> `if (CornerFreq <= 0)` -- survived the inherited 4468-case corpus. It was NOT equivalent, and that was proved rather than argued: the two predicates disagree on exactly one input, `CornerFreq == 0`, they are bit-identical at +0.0 (0 of 36 draws differ) and they differ at -0.0 in `FP%nfs_b2` (36 of 36, `8000000000000000` against `0000000000000000`). THE GATE SEES THIS UNIT, AND SEES FEWER THAN HALF OF ITS OUTPUTS. It is the first unit in this campaign where those two statements are both true, and the second is the larger finding: 23 of the 43 fields `ReadAvrSWAP` writes are invisible to the kernel AND to the gate at once.

MEASURED WITH ONE STUB, THREE WAYS. `evidence/ReadAvrSWAP/readavrswap.zero-fed-outputs-deleted-stub.cpp` deletes the whole `IF (CntrPar%Ext_Interface > 0)` block -- 18 `Ptfm*` assignments -- plus `VS_MechGenPwr`, `FA_Acc_TT`, `SS_Acc_TT`, `NacIMU_FA_RAcc` and `FA_Acc_Nac`. The kernel scores it 62 of 62 IDENTICAL; disabling the same block at the gate moves 0 of 5,252,000 with all 27 scenarios alive (evidence/ReadAvrSWAP/gate.ext-interface-block-disabled-MOVES-NOTHING.json) on the build whose `GenSpeed` perturbation moves 1,487,557; the differential harness fails it 26,198 of 26,198 and names the fields.

THREE MECHANISMS, AND ONLY ONE OF THEM IS REPAIRABLE BY WIDENING THE SCENARIOS.
  1. NO DATA. `avrSWAP(14)`, `(54)` and `(1001..1018)` are written by nothing in this tree. `rosco/toolbox/control_interface.py` allocates `np.zeros(3000)` and writes 24 indices, none of them these; the scenarios add six more, none of them these. `Ext_Interface = 1` in all 14 `Examples/DISCON*.IN` and coverage puts the block at 443,972 executions, so it is a real input surface that a Python driver emulating ServoDyn simply does not supply.
  2. DATA WRITTEN AND THEN OVERWRITTEN. Scenario 27 sets `controller_int.avrSWAP[52]` (tower-top acceleration, for its `TD_Mode = 1`) and `[82]` (nacelle IMU, for its `Fl_Mode = 2`) and then calls `call_controller`, whose first act is a block of `self.avrSWAP[...] =` assignments including `except KeyError: self.avrSWAP[82] = 0` against a `turbine_state` carrying neither key. Both injections are zeroed before the DLL is called; scenarios 7 and 26 lose the same two the same way. `FA_Acc_Nac` is the field to keep in view: its readers are live and unconditional (`Filters.f90:372`, `:395`), so it is invisible ONLY because both of its inputs are zero.
  3. NO READER THE GATE READS. The 18 `Ptfm*` fields have no consumer in the controller at all: outside this assignment they appear only in `ROSCO_IO`'s debug `WRITE`, its restart-file `READ` and the `LocalVarOutData` table, and `gate.py` compares `baseline_arrays`, never a `.RO.dbg`. `VS_MechGenPwr` adds `ZeroMQInterface`, and `ZMQ_Mode` is 0 in all 14 inputs. For those 19, fixing (1) would not help.
NOT FIXED HERE, deliberately: repairing (2) changes what the 27 scenarios feed the controller, which moves `baseline_arrays` and the compared count -- X3 and SPEC 8.4, the Driver's call. Recorded in DECISIONS.md as a candidate.

COST PAID TO REACH 1.000, and it is a finding about the INSTRUMENT in two parts.
  (a) A LADDER AIMED AT A NAME IS NOT A LADDER OVER THE QUANTITY. The unit branches four times on `LocalVar%iStatus == 0`, `LocalVar_iStatus` IS a scalar integer parameter, and unit #10's integer decade ladder gave it 0 -- and every one of those cases was DEAD, because the unit's first statement is `LocalVar%iStatus = NINT(avrSWAP(1))`. The deciding value arrives as one ELEMENT of an array, and `_fill_array` gives an array a single ascending ramp, so `avrSWAP(1)` is about -999 in every case the generator has ever produced. Same for `NINT(avrSWAP(61))` -> `NumBl` and `avrSWAP(2)` -> `Time`. The corpus contained the value and could not reach the branch: the tenth corpus blind spot here and the first of that shape.
  (b) TWO LADDERS THAT NEVER CROSS CANNOT REACH A BRANCH THAT NEEDS BOTH. Every generator stage sets ONE parameter and leaves the rest at base, and `flag_variants` crosses only DECLARED flags -- of which this signature has exactly one, `LocalVar_restart`, which the reference overwrites unconditionally. The pitch-fault loop needs `PF_Mode == 1` AND `NumBl >= 2` AND `iStatus /= 0` in the SAME case; each was individually reachable and the conjunction was not.
Closed by ADDITION: `predicate_knobs_from` reads the reference's own predicates and follows each tested name back to the element it ENTERS by, and generate.py's R7 block emits the cross product -- 729 combinations of six quantities, 26,198 -> 27,656 cases, bounded at 4096 with an all-pairs fallback that reports itself. Appended last, so no earlier unit's corpus moves.

The two differ on exactly one input, a capacity of 58, and the capacity is `LEN(ErrMsg) + 4096` in the harness (`harness/emit.py`) and in the integrated build (`vit_errorvariables_view.f90:63`) alike. Same site, same reason, same declaration as ExtController's `11d2c9cc`. The guard is what makes an over-long assignment a REFUSAL rather than a truncation, and a truncated error message is the one wrong answer a bit comparison cannot catch, so it is not deleted to raise a score.

WHAT THE KERNEL CANNOT SEE BEYOND THAT: the already-loaded branch. Coverage of the clean source puts `IF (LocalVar%AlreadyInitialized == 0)` at 28 hits, its TRUE branch at 28 and its ELSE branch -- the two statements writing `aviFAIL` and `ErrMsg` -- at ZERO in all 27 scenarios. THE GATE IS BLIND TO THIS UNIT, AND THE REFERENCE IS BLIND TO ITSELF ON SIX OF ITS TEN OUTPUTS. The second is the finding.

WHICH BODY WAS TRANSLATED. `ZeroMQInterface.f90` is written twice, under `#ifdef ZMQ_CLIENT` and `#else`. rosco/controller/CMakeLists.txt:131 gates the definition on `pkg_check_modules(PC_ZeroMQ libzmq)` and this tree's CMakeCache records `PC_ZeroMQ_FOUND:INTERNAL=` -- empty. ZMQ_CLIENT is UNDEFINED, `zmq_client` is neither compiled nor linked, and the `#else` branch is the object under translation.

THE REFERENCE IS NOT A FUNCTION OF ITS ARGUMENTS ON `LocalVar%ZMQ_TorqueOffset`, `ZMQ_YawOffset`, `ZMQ_PitOffset(1:3)`, `ZMQ_R_Speed`, `ZMQ_R_Torque` and `ZMQ_R_Pitch`. `real(C_DOUBLE) :: setpoints(8)` is never assigned in this configuration and the procedure copies it into those eight fields. Measured twice, from both sides: three calls in one process return NaN and denormals on a fresh frame, then 1.0 after a routine that fills the same stack region with 1.0, then -7.25 after one that fills it with -7.25 (evidence/UpdateZeroMQ/setpoints_indeterminate.run.txt); and the first generated harness run had 4,175 of 4,179 cases agreeing on every output with 4 disagreeing on these fields alone, the reference answering a leftover pointer (evidence/UpdateZeroMQ/harness.setpoints-indeterminate-FAILS-4-of-4179.json). They are declared `no_oracle` in harness/ranges.toml, reported in the run's own artifact rather than applied silently. THE COST: nothing constrains what the translation writes there, and 7 of the 8 declared-equivalent mutants are unkillable for that single reason. WHAT REMAINS CONSTRAINED, and it is not nothing: `aviFAIL`, `ErrMsg`, and the two predicates that decide whether either is written.

THE GATE. Both call sites are dead in all 27 scenarios (guard hits 407,976 and 36,024, CALL hits 0 and 0), so a whole-unit no-op moves 0 of 5,252,000. A same-build control moves 1,857,893, so this is unit #1's dead-unit shape rather than a broken chain. Even if a scenario drove it, three of the eight outputs have no consumer in the controller at all -- `ZMQ_TorqueOffset` appears only in ROSCO_IO's debug WRITE, the restart READ and the LocalVarOutData table -- and the other five reach `PitCom`, `NacVaneOffset` and `PRC_R_*` only under `ZMQ_Mode == 1` or `PRC_Comm == PRC_Comm_ZMQ`.

WHAT NO LAYER SEES BECAUSE THE DOMAIN IS PINNED, stated rather than left to be found. `CntrPar_ZMQ_CommAddress` is held at one value because a full-width address ABORTS the reference: field and local are both CHARACTER(256) and the internal write needs LEN_TRIM+1 = 257 (`Fortran runtime error: End of record`, exit 2, evidence/UpdateZeroMQ/domain_aborts.run.txt). Nothing here can tell a translation that reads the address from one that ignores it -- which costs less than it would anywhere else, since in this configuration the reference writes it into a local only the uncompiled `zmq_client` call would read. `MOD(n_DT, 0)` is the second such shape: `n_DT_ZMQ = NINT(ZMQ_UpdatePeriod/DT)` and `ZMQ_UpdatePeriod` is only parsed when `ZMQ_Mode /= 0`, so the divisor is 0 on every input this campaign carries, and the `ZMQ_Mode > 0` guard is the only thing between the shipped controller and a division by zero.

THREE STATEMENTS OF THE REFERENCE ARE NOT TRANSCRIBED, each with its proof in the translation's header: the 17 `turbine_measurements` dead stores (nothing reads the array in this configuration), the `write` to `zmq_address` (dead within the admissible domain, aborting outside it), and the TRIM in `ErrVar%ErrMsg = RoutineName//':'//TRIM(ErrVar%ErrMsg)` (it reads a literal the previous statement just assigned). The first two are unit #4's rule about restatements; the third was found by the mutation score, where its four sites survived as unobservable mutants.

units.observability:
THE GATE SEES THIS UNIT ALMOST EVERYWHERE, AND THE KERNEL SEES ONE VALUE OF ITS ONLY INPUT. Both are properties of the same fact: `identity(3)` is called from one place, inside the wind-speed estimator's Kalman measurement update (`LocalVar%WE%P = MATMUL(identity(3) - MATMUL(K,H), P)`), 330,797 times across 22 of the 27 scenarios.

GATE-VISIBLE, and by the widest margin so far: 1,462,798 of 5,252,000 values across 115 of 351 channels -- blade pitch, generator speed/torque/power, flap angle and nacelle yaw -- in every scenario except 10, 13, 14, 17 and 24, which are the ones STATUS.md has carried since phase 3 as executing no controller code. The covariance feeds the estimated wind speed, which feeds the pitch and torque schedules, so a wrong identity matrix is a different simulation.

WHAT NO SIMULATION-BASED LAYER CONSTRAINS: the argument. `n` is the literal 3 at the only call site, in every scenario, forever. A constant stub passes the kernel 13,950 of 13,950 and would pass the gate too. Everything this campaign knows about `identity` AS A FUNCTION OF n comes from 29 differential cases at five values of it.

TWO THINGS ARE UNFALSIFIABLE HERE RATHER THAN UNTESTED, and the difference matters:
  * COLUMN-MAJOR vs ROW-MAJOR. Transposing the index expression moves 0 of 29 cases at every n, because the identity matrix is SYMMETRIC. No corpus can distinguish them. VIT's own column-major check is enforced on this translation and cannot be tested by it.
  * THE KERNEL'S VERDICT. Not `the window is vacuous` (it is not -- `p` is order 1 and a wrong constant scores 0/62) but `a NaN output is scored IN_TOL`. Every unit whose failure mode is NaN has the same hole, and this is the first one to produce a NaN and be measured.

WHAT THE MUTATION SCORE DOES NOT COVER: the stride multiplier, for a syntactic reason with nothing to do with this unit -- `cppmutate` cannot mutate a parenthesised operand, and the parenthesis is required by VIT's own `exponent-grouping` check. Two hand-run probes kill on 2 of 29 each. The score is 1.000 of what was generated, and what was generated is 20 mutants of a 9-line function.

bridge_feasible.basis: MEASURED, replacing the matrix-derived `unknown`, and BOTH generators cross it -- but the differential one needed two fixes and one stated judgement before it could run a single case. `vit interface` emits `REAL(C_DOUBLE), INTENT(IN) :: xData(*)` plus `INTEGER(C_INT), VALUE :: n_xData` for each assumed-shape array and `TYPE(C_PTR), VALUE :: ErrVar` for the derived type; it builds, links, and the gate's red test moves 1,341,803 values through it. What it does NOT do by default is copy the view back: see `verification`, and note that the flag is not optional for this unit. `test_validate.generate_fortran_bridge` compiles the same signature unchanged. The LOOP's generator did not: `relational_pairs_from` matched `IF (xq <= xData(I))` and reported the array side with NO index -- indistinguishable from `the predicate names the parameter` -- and `_pin` then wrote a scalar over an array parameter, `TypeError: 'float' object is not iterable` out of `emit.write_cases`, with no case file written. Fixed by ADDITION in harness/generate.py: an array side with an unresolved subscript pins an INTERIOR element. The judgement is `harness/ranges.toml`'s third kind of entry, `same_as`, and it exists because the REFERENCE has no answer: `SIZE(xData) /= SIZE(yData)` reallocates ErrMsg to 38 characters and then formats 53 into it -- `End of record`, exit 2, measured (evidence/interp1d/reference.size-mismatch-aborts.txt). `_extent_plan` makes extents pairwise distinct on purpose, so every case killed the oracle until the two were tied.

units.observability:
THE GATE SEES THIS UNIT WIDELY AND THE KERNEL SEES ONE THIRD OF IT, AND THE WRAPPER TURNED OUT TO SEE NONE OF WHAT IT WRITES TO ErrVar.

GATE-VISIBLE: 1,341,803 of 5,252,000 values move under a x1.000001 perturbation of the return value. `interp1d` has 24 call sites, and the live ones are the pitch controller's gain schedule (`PC_GS_angles` -> KP/KI/KD/TF, 407,976 calls), the wind-speed estimator's first-order pole (330,797), the peak-shaving minimum-pitch schedule (391,977) and the floating feedback gain (79,996). Every one of those feeds blade pitch or generator torque directly.

WHAT THE KERNEL CANNOT SEE, and it is two thirds of the control flow rather than an argument: both ENDPOINT branches. A stub with `xq <= MINVAL(xData)` and `xq >= MAXVAL(xData)` deleted passes 62 of 62 with 248 of 248 rows IDENTICAL, because every query captured at ControllerBlocks.f90:421 falls inside the table. Also invisible: both error branches and the RoutineName prefix -- `avifail` is 0 in all 62 captured cases, so the whole `IF (ErrVar%aviFAIL < 0)` tail is unentered. Everything this campaign knows about those five paths comes from 497 differential cases.

WHAT NO INSTRUMENT CAN CONSTRAIN, because the reference has no answer there: the `SIZE(xData) /= SIZE(yData)` branch. The reference ABORTS in it (exit 2, `End of record`), so a comparison cannot be written at all; `harness/ranges.toml` ties the two extents and states the cost, which includes any defect that needs the extents to DIFFER -- a translation reading `n_yData` where the reference reads `SIZE(xData)` agrees on every case here.

AND ONE THING THAT WAS INVISIBLE TO EVERY SIMULATION-BASED LAYER AT ONCE: the wrapper's reverse copy. The first integration dropped this unit's writes to `ErrVar%aviFAIL` and `ErrVar%ErrMsg` and both the kernel and the 27-scenario gate passed it, because the scenarios hand `interp1d` well-formed monotone tables and `aviFAIL == 0`. Only the post-integration differential harness could see it. That is the sharpest form so far of `a unit the gate cannot see is not a unit the gate passed` -- here the gate DID see the unit, 1.3 million values wide, and was still blind to an entire output.

THE CORPUS BLIND SPOT THIS UNIT CLOSED (R10, the fifteenth): a predicate whose OTHER SIDE is a REDUCTION of a varied array has no name to pin -- its crossing value is not in the case stream at all, it is whatever `_fill_array` drew. `xq <= MINVAL(xData)` against `<` and `xq >= MAXVAL(xData)` against `>` differ on exactly one input each, and 473 cases produced neither. R10 draws the array body first, computes the reduction, and sets the scalar to it and to its two neighbouring representable numbers, over the body and its REVERSE so the extremum is once first and once last.

Counts are over the ELSE arm, which is where the arithmetic is.

  the return value == a bound        2307 of 2307      3568 of 4884
  minValue < maxValue at all          207 of 2307      4884 of 4884
  EFilt finite                          1 of 2307      1507 of 4884
  the outer clamp INACTIVE              0 of 2307      1316 of 4884
  the ITerm clamp INACTIVE              8 of 2307      4285 of 4884
  both clamps inactive at once          0 of 2307      1313 of 4884

TWO INDEPENDENT CAUSES, AND FIXING EITHER ALONE LEAVES THE ZERO AT ZERO.
  (1) `LPFilter` divides by `FP%lpf1_a1(inst)` (Filters.f90:65), written only inside `IF ((iStatus == 0) .OR. reset)`, and the harness supplies `LocalVar%FP` ZEROED on every case -- so EFilt is `1.0/0.0 * 0.0` = NaN wherever iStatus /= 0 and reset is false, and NaN swamps the sum. `iStatus` was an ordinary defaulted integer on R6's decade ladder, which reaches 0 once in 2307 cases.
  (2) `minValue` and `maxValue` are drawn INDEPENDENTLY from the same default, so the pair that has to be an interval came out (0, -300) in 1512 of 2307 cases -- and R6's isolating stage, which pins every OTHER defaulted real to one value, sets them EQUAL, which is the same empty interval by another route. `saturate(x, lo, hi)` is `MIN(MAX(x,lo),hi)` and returns `hi` for every x once lo >= hi.

THE REMEDY IS THREE ENTRIES IN harness/ranges.toml, per-unit, and NOT a change to the shared generator -- which is what X3 forbids mid-run and what R15_bracketing_bounds in DECISIONS.md still specifies for the generator. `LocalVar_iStatus` to the reference's own documented enumeration [0, 1, -1] with 0 first; `minValue` to [-1e9, -1e-3] and `maxValue` to [1e-3, 1e9], which is the only call site's own shape (Controllers.f90:346 passes -LocalVar%VS_MaxTq*2 and +LocalVar%VS_MaxTq*2) widened, with the magnitude taken from the clamped sum itself (|raw| median 2994, 90th percentile 1.86e6).     zeroed, every iStatus /= 0 case answers NaN -- 3377 of 4884 -- so what the
    corpus exercises is the INIT arm and the propagation of NaN, never a filter
    with state. Reaching it needs a non-zero FP, and FP is a NESTED type the
    generator does not vary. That is a generator gap, recorded in DECISIONS.md;
    a range cannot state it.
  the outer clamp is ACTIVE in 3568 of 4884, which is the arm being kept rather
    than a loss -- but a defect visible ONLY when the clamp is active and the
    bracket INVERTED (lo > hi) is now unreachable, because both bounds are
    pinned to opposite signs. That defect would be in `saturate`, which is unit
    #24 and is CALLED, not inlined, so both sides of this comparison reach one

    167 fields, and this unit reads two of them). A defect confined to a held
    parameter is invisible.

    varied, and compared BYTEWISE after the call. So LPFilter's writes are seen

product of the ten quantities its own predicates test is 552,960, past

the FIRST value of its ladder -- and `ErrVar_aviFAIL`'s ladder is [-1, 0, 1, 2].

293), but it does not move the other 8740 and this is stated rather than left to

somewhere in those 293.

THE KERNEL PASSES A STUB THAT FORCES EVERY `reset` ARGUMENT TO FALSE, AND IT IS
AN EQUIVALENCE IN THE WHOLE PROGRAM RATHER THAN A CORPUS GAP. Two greps, not a
case count:

  Filters.f90 (clean, 54dd134): all five filters guard their initialisation with
      IF ((iStatus == 0) .OR. reset)
  ReadSetParameters.f90:123-126 is the ONLY assignment to LocalVar%restart in
  the whole controller:
      IF (LocalVar%iStatus == 0) THEN ; LocalVar%restart = .True. ; ELSE .False.

So `reset` is TRUE only where `iStatus == 0` already is, and the `.OR.` makes
the second term redundant at all nineteen of this unit's call sites. In the
captured window it is visible directly -- `restart` is T in 1 of 62 cases and
`istatus` is 0 in exactly that one -- and the stub passes 62 of 62 with ZERO
rows moved. It would pass at any window and in any of the 27 scenarios, and it
predicts the gate is blind to that argument too. The differential harness is
what is NOT blind: it draws `iStatus` and `restart` independently and so reaches
the (iStatus /= 0, reset = .TRUE.) corner the program never builds.

THREE ARMS ARE OUTSIDE EVERY BIT-EXACT INSTRUMENT, read from coverage rather
than argued (clean-source line numbers):

  :379       DO n = 1,F_TwrTopNotch_N                    the DO line carries
                                                         exactly the call count
                                                         in every scenario, so
                                                         the body iterates 0 times
  :406-:417  the Flp_Mode == 2 blade-root arm            scenario 4 ONLY

The kernel's 62 cases confirm the first three at the value level: f_lpftype is 1
in 62 of 62, f_twrtopnotch_n is 0 in 62 of 62, flp_mode is 0 in 62 of 62, and
ipc_controlmode is 1 in 62 of 62 -- so the `RootMOOPF(K) = rootMOOP(K)` ELSE arm
is never taken there either. The differential harness reaches all of them, and
its R11 baseline states BOTH configurations for that reason: state

inspection:

  confined to one of them is invisible here.

THE RESET ARM IS OUTSIDE EVERY BIT-EXACT INSTRUMENT BUT ONE, AND THE ONE THAT REACHES IT HAS NO ANSWER FOR THE RETURN VALUE.

`ResController` assigns its own result in the ELSE arm only (Controllers.f90:1215-1223, clean). On `IF (reset)` it writes four resP elements and returns whatever the result slot holds; the caller assigns that to `AWC_TiltYaw(Imode)`, which feeds the inverse Coleman transform and every blade's pitch command. That is upstream ROSCO's defect, the fifth this campaign has recorded, and it is not something a translation can mirror.

THREE INSTRUMENTS, THREE ANSWERS ABOUT THAT ARM:
  * the kernel is BLIND to it. `localvar%restart` is F in 62 of 62 captured cases, and a stub that empties the arm entirely passes 62 of 62 (evidence/ResController/kernel.reset-arm-stub.run.txt).
  * the gate is BLIND to it, MEASURED rather than inferred from coverage. Perturbing the first of the four writes moves 0 of 5,252,000 values, revert-verified -- gate/ResController.redtest.reset-arm.json, verdict RED_TEST_FAIL. Coverage agrees from the other side: those four lines have zero hits in all 27 scenarios. `LocalVar%restart = (iStatus == 0)` is the only assignment to it in the controller and the AWC block sits behind `IF (LocalVar%Time .GT. StartTime)`, false at iStatus == 0, so nothing in these scenarios can enter the arm.
  * the differential harness DOES reach it -- 1464 of 2925 cases -- which is why `reset` was kept two-valued rather than pinned away. What it cannot compare there is the RETURN VALUE, and that is stated as `vit_result = { no_oracle = ... }` in harness/ranges.toml. The first run of this corpus failed 1763 of 3532 on that one output alone, the reference returning byte patterns that change from case to case (evidence/ResController/harness.UNDEFINED-RESULT-3532.json).

THE COST OF THAT EXCLUSION, STATED: the harness no longer compares the return value on ANY case, including the 1461 where the reference does define it. It costs little because the ELSE arm stores the returned value into `res_OutputSignalLast1(inst)` (Controllers.f90:1223), which IS compared on every case -- so the arithmetic is not excluded, only the copy of it that leaves through the return. Two other instruments do compare that copy: the kernel replays 62 cases through the CALLER, where the result lands in `AWC_TiltYaw`, and the gate runs the whole program. What is genuinely uncovered is a translation that returns something OTHER than what it stores, on the reset path only.

TWO INPUT DOMAINS WERE NARROWED, both to remove a blindness rather than to avoid a crash. On the +/-1e3 default `saturate(x, lo, hi)` returned a bound in all but about twelve of 3532 cases -- the mutation kill counts are the census and they are bimodal (evidence/ResController/mutation.CLAMPED-CORPUS-3532.txt) -- so `minValue` and `maxValue` are pinned to the call site's own shape widened, PC_MinPit/PC_MaxPit. The cost is R6's magnitude ladder and its isolating stage for those two, and an INVERTED bracket, which would exercise `saturate` -- unit #24, CALLED not inlined, so both sides of this comparison reach one implementation of it and this harness never constrained it.

THE GATE SEES THE UNIT. 280,312 of 5,252,000 values move when the unit produces no output, revert-verified. Only three of the 27 scenarios reach it at all (5 and 8 at 15,998 calls, 27 at 23,998), all AWC_Mode == 4.

MORE THAN HALF OF THIS UNIT IS OUTSIDE EVERY SIMULATION THE CAMPAIGN RUNS, AND THE DIFFERENTIAL HARNESS NEEDED THIRTEEN BASELINE STATES TO REACH IT.

Scenario 9 is the only one of the 27 that calls Shutdown -- 11,999 invocations, 0 in the other 26. Within those, coverage records SD_Trigger = 1, 2 and 3 at ZERO hits against one hit for SD_Trigger = 4; the stage never advances past 1; and the whole SD_Method == 2 arm never runs. The gate's second red test confirmed the last of those from the other side: 0 of 5,252,000.

THE GENERATED CORPUS COULD NOT REACH THOSE ARMS EITHER, AND THE REASON IS UNIT #37's. Every statement that writes this unit's two principal outputs needs a TRIPLE -- SD_Method in {1,2} AND SD_Stage /= 0 AND SD_Stage <= SD_Stage_N -- and R6's coverage line reads `283 combination(s) ... ALL PAIRS ONLY -- the full cross product is 186624, past the 4096 bound`, which holds every knob not being crossed at its ladder's FIRST value. SD_Method's first value is 0: neither method. Measured, not argued: on the corpus with no baseline, 29 of 109 mutants survived and every non-equivalent survivor was a subscript of one of the four SD_ allocatables.

Closed by ADDITION -- 13 states in harness/baseline.Shutdown.json, taking the corpus from 14253 to 14708 cases and the mutation score from 0.734 to 1.000. Two states enter the two stage machines; three isolate one shutdown trigger each (the four trigger tests are independent IFs, so the LAST one that fires wins and the earlier constants are unobservable); five sit ON an equality that `>` and `>=` disagree about; and one reaches the negative side of the yaw test, without which dropping ABS() changes nothing.

TWO OF THE THRESHOLD BOUNDARIES LOOKED UNREACHABLE AND ARE NOT. `SD_GenSpeedF > SD_MaxGenSpd` and `ABS(SD_NacVaneF) > SD_MaxYawError` compare a value this unit COMPUTES against one it is given, so R6's relational-pair rule -- which needs both sides to be inputs -- cannot put them at equality. LPFilter's initialisation arm returns its input BIT-EXACTLY when CornerFreq is 0 (its coefficients become 2, -2, 0, 0 and the expression collapses to (1/2)*(2x), both operations exact), so setting the corner frequency to zero with iStatus = 0 turns the computed side back into an input. Both mutants are killed rather than declared.

WHAT IS STILL NOT REACHED: the ErrMsg staging boundary. R13_staging_capacity sweeps the capacity 0..255 across 256 cases, and every one of them takes its other inputs at the BASE DRAW, where ErrVar%aviFAIL is not negative and the refusal guard is never entered. The census says the same from the value side -- n_ErrMsg_cap is 4103 in all 3565 calls that DO reach it. The rule that exists to sweep this capacity and the arm that reads it are disjoint. That is a finding about the instrument, and it is three of this unit's twelve declarations.

THE ARM THIS UNIT EXISTS FOR IS OUTSIDE EVERY SIMULATION THE CAMPAIGN RUNS, AND THE REASON IS NOT THAT NO SCENARIO CONFIGURES IT.

coverage/line_coverage.json records Controllers.f90:1003-1012 -- the whole StC_Mode == 2 open-loop arm, this unit's only call to interp1d and the only reader of Ind_StructControl, OL_Breakpoints and OL_StructControl -- at ZERO hits in all 27 scenarios. The gate's second red test confirms it from the other side: disabling the arm moves 0 of 5,252,000 compared values, revert-verified.

Examples/vit_sim.py scenario 24 DOES configure it: StC_Mode = 2, StC_Group_N = 1, StC_GroupIndex 2801, Ind_StructControl 8, OL_Mode = 1. It is the one scenario in this campaign built for exactly this arm. It never reaches DISCON's main block -- coverage puts 0 hits on DISCON.F90:136 (the IF (StC_Mode > 0) guard) under scenario 24 while DISCON.F90:141 carries 8,000, so all 8,000 of its calls fall through to the ELSEIF. Units #23 and #26 measured the cause and STATUS.md has carried it since phase 3 as an E3.3 failure: Read_OL_Input takes its RETURN on the absent Examples/example_inputs/OL_Mode2_Input.dat. Reading the guard alone would have recorded "no scenario configures it"; reading the scenario records "one scenario configures it and a missing FILE stops the whole controller". Only the second decides whether widening the scenarios could help.

THE ERROR-MESSAGE PREFIX IS LIKEWISE AT ZERO HITS IN ALL 27, and so is the whole Time <= 500 side of the step in scenario 3.

WHAT CLOSED IT was the differential harness, and it needed a rewrite and a baseline rather than only more cases. The first sweep scored 0.810 with eleven survivors in exactly two places. FOUR of them were a DEFENSIVE GUARD this translation had and the reference does not -- `std::vector<double> row(cols > 0 ? (size_t)cols : 0)` tests a quantity R5 never draws below 3, so all three mutants of the test spell `cols`, and passing `cols` rather than the buffer's own length as SIZE(yData) hid a fourth that writes past the vector. The site was rewritten, not declared. THREE more were unreached: R6 crosses StC_Mode = 2 with StC_Group_N = 1 at the full cross product, but nothing makes Ind_StructControl(1) positive, because that subscript is the loop counter and the generator's own note says it is not traceable to a parameter. harness/baseline.StructuralControl.json's first state ramps Ind_StructControl from exactly 1 -- which is also where the '> 0' -> '> 1' survivor changes an answer -- and kills all three.

WHAT IS STILL NOT REACHED, and it is the same finding unit #41 recorded: the ErrMsg helpers' three boundaries. A supplied length of exactly 1, a supplied length of 0 or less, and a message whose length equals the staging capacity. All three are properties of ErrVar%ErrMsg's LENGTH, and `_baseline_state` deliberately leaves every CHARACTER parameter to R6's own ladder, so no state in this file can move them. R13_staging_capacity DID run -- 256 cases sweeping the headroom 0..255 -- and not one of them is among the 120 cases that reach the helpers, because every R13 case takes its other inputs at the BASE DRAW where aviFAIL is not negative. The rule that exists to sweep this capacity and the arm that reads it are disjoint. Measured: evidence/StructuralControl/errmsg_census.txt.

THREE RANGE PINS NARROW THE DOMAIN and each states its cost in harness/ranges.toml: StC_Group_N to 0..3 (it bounds both loops and bounds none of the four arrays they subscript), StC_GroupIndex to 1..3000 (its VALUE is an avrSWAP subscript and avrSWAP is an assumed-size dummy the reference cannot bounds-check), and OL_StructControl's COLUMN count tied to OL_Breakpoints_n (interp1d dies on a size mismatch). units.observability:
THE REFERENCE READS OUT OF BOUNDS ON A TABLE IT HAS JUST REPORTED AS MALFORMED, AND THAT ONE FACT SETS THIS UNIT'S DOMAIN AND EXPLAINS HALF ITS SURVIVORS.

`interp2d` checks that xData and yData are strictly increasing, sets aviFAIL = -1, writes a message -- and then interpolates anyway. On a DESCENDING table every interior query satisfies `xq < xData(1)` at the first iteration, so the corner search exits with jj = 1, `j = j - 1 = 0`, and `zData(i, 0)` is one column before the array. The reference reads what precedes ITS buffer and the translation reads what precedes ITS OWN. Six cases of 1117 reached it and five disagreed, every mismatch on vit_result and none on any other output (evidence/interp2d/harness.out-of-bounds-corner-census.txt). Unit #41's rule: a red result that is really an undefined reference cannot be told from a translation defect, and vit_mutate.py refuses to score against a red baseline, so nothing downstream could have closed either.

`harness/ranges.toml` gained a FOURTH judgement kind for it, `ordered_only`, which takes an array out of BOTH rules that leave the ascending domain -- R6's ordering sweep and R10's reversed body. Excluding the ladder alone moved 5 failures to 4; R10's reverse was the rest. 1117 -> 1005 cases, 0 failed.

AND THAT EXCLUSION WAS ONE SHAPE TOO WIDE, WHICH THE SWEEP MEASURED BEFORE ANYONE ARGUED IT. What the reference cannot survive is an INVERSION, not a tie. Its search runs only in the arm where `xq > MINVAL(xData)`, and on a NON-DECREASING body `MINVAL(xData)` IS `xData(1)` -- so the first iteration falls through, `jj` is never 1, and `zData(i, 0)` cannot arise. An inverted body is exactly what breaks that identity: its minimum is not its first element and a query between the two subscripts one column early, which is the shape of all 6 out-of-bounds reads the census found. A FIFTH judgement kind, `nondecreasing_only` (translation-loop c7869e8), keeps the ladder and drops the reversed and pair-inverted shapes; R10 pins its reduction over the non-decreasing shapes rather than over the reverse. 1005 -> 1147 cases, 0 failed, and 17 of the unit's 32 surviving mutants died to it. WHAT IS STILL GIVEN UP is the whole of the cost now: `MINVAL(xData)` written as `xData(1)` still has no dynamic witness, and no case has a table whose first element is not its minimum -- which is why two survivors stand.

AND THE COST OF THAT EXCLUSION WAS STATED WRONG, AND THE MUTATION SWEEP SAID SO. The entry claimed the ordinary random draws would still reach the two checks "one time in six". `harness/generate._fill_array` draws STRICTLY INCREASING bodies by construction, so once the exclusions are in, no case in the corpus has a non-increasing table at all -- and the refutation is in the artifact rather than in a re-reading: `ErrVar->aviFAIL = -1` inside the lambda those checks alone call, mutated to `-2`, SURVIVED, while aviFAIL is compared on every one of the 1005 cases. 14 of the 32 survivors live in that dead code. The wrong sentence is kept in ranges.toml beside its correction (C12).

TWO EXTENT TIES, the same shape as interp1d's and for a sharper reason. `n_zData_cols` follows `n_xData` and `n_zData_rows` follows `n_yData`, because the reference's two size-mismatch branches format 59 characters into `ErrVar%ErrMsg` AS IT STANDS -- there is no literal assignment in front of the WRITE, unlike interp1d's -- and DISCON.F90:159 leaves that field at LEN 0. Measured in isolation: "Fortran runtime error: End of record", exit 2 (evidence/interp2d/reference.size-mismatch-aborts.txt). The two branches and the 2 mutants inside them are unreachable here. ROWS AND COLS ARE TIED TO DIFFERENT PARTNERS ON PURPOSE, so they stay distinct from each other: a translation that strode this column-major array by the column count instead of the row count still disagrees on every case, which is the property R5's pairwise distinctness exists to protect.

`yq` NaN HAS AN ORACLE, AND THE PARAGRAPH THAT STOOD HERE WAS THE DEFECT ITSELF. It read: "The x-direction guards with `ieee_is_nan(xq)`; the y-direction does not... the reference has no answer." That is a true description of the TRANSLATION written as though it were a reading of the reference. `Functions.f90` at the clean baseline guards BOTH searches -- lines 231 and 257, `grep -c ieee_is_nan` is 2 -- so on `yq` NaN with `xq` interior the reference returns `interp1d(xData, zData(1,:), xq)` and the translation ran the y-loop to completion and read `ii` unwritten. All four instruments passed it: no case draws a NaN query, a mutation sweep grades the corpus against the translation rather than against the reference, and no gate scenario sends a NaN into a Cp/Ct/Cq lookup. Fixed at 7639168f; recorded first, with the wrong artifact quoted, in evidence/interp2d/yq-nan-guard.MISTRANSLATION.md (C12). WITH BOTH GUARDS IN, NO INDEX IS EVER READ UNWRITTEN: a NaN query returns at the first test in its own direction, and a non-NaN query strictly inside the extrema always reaches an EXIT because some element exceeds it.

THE GATE STILL SEES NO ERROR PATH, AND THE HARNESS NOW SEES TWO OF THE FOUR. The two strictly-increasing checks are live in the corpus at 1147 cases and were dead at 1005; the two size-mismatch branches remain unreachable and unreachable-in-principle for a differential instrument, because the reference's own WRITE ends the process there.

SIX OF THE REFERENCE'S TEN INDEX ASSIGNMENTS ARE DEAD AND ARE NOT TRANSCRIBED. Every `jj = ...` and `ii = ...` standing immediately before one of the five RETURNs writes a subroutine local nothing reads afterwards. That is unit #43's rule applied BEFORE the sweep rather than after -- six dead stores would have been six survivors with nothing to say -- and their liveness is a property of the reference rather than a reading of it. The `j = ...` and `i = ...` of the same branches ARE live (they subscript the slice being passed on) and are kept. Same reasoning retires the reference's `fQ(2,2)` staging array and its one-element `fxy`, whose only mutants are out-of-bounds subscripts.

THE GATE SEES THIS UNIT WELL. 391,882 of its 676,656 calls in all 27 scenarios reach the bilinear path, and scaling that result by 1.000001 moves 922,411 of 5,252,000 compared values. What the gate does NOT constrain is the error handling: its 27 scenarios hand interp2d well-formed monotone Cp/Ct/Cq tables read from a performance file, so no scenario enters any of the four error paths.
